description: Engineers automated release pipelines, Cloud Infrastructure as Code (IaC), Kubernetes container platforms, observability, and incident recovery.
default_interviewer_tone: Direct, operational, reliability-focused; probes for failure modes, rollback strategies, infrastructure drift, and incident resolution.

question_style_notes.entry: Verbal problem-solving on Dockerfile layering, basic CI script syntax, and Linux permission debugging. No assumption of multi-region production clusters.
question_style_notes.mid: Terraform state locks and drift, zero-downtime blue/green releases, Kubernetes pod eviction causes, and alert routing.
question_style_notes.senior: Multi-cluster service meshes, disaster recovery failovers, cost governance, infrastructure security policies, and post-mortem incident response.
question_style_notes.lead: Platform engineering strategy, SLO/error budget governance, chaos engineering adoption, and compliance automation.

skills.name: CI/CD & Release Engineering
skills.description: Builds automated build/test pipelines, container image signing, canary and blue/green deployments, and automated rollbacks.
skills.rubric_l1: Deploys manual tarballs/FTP directly to servers; no automated tests or version control release triggers.
skills.rubric_l2: Configures basic GitHub Actions or Jenkins jobs for build/test but lacks environment promotion, secrets management, or automated rollbacks.
skills.rubric_l3: Builds secure CI/CD pipelines with immutable container tags, environment gates, automated smoke tests, and rollback triggers.
skills.rubric_l4: Implements progressive canary deployments (ArgoCD/Flagger), cryptographic image provenance (Cosign), and automated SLO burn verification.
skills.rubric_l5: Architects enterprise-wide ephemeral preview environments, trunk-based release automation, and supply chain security frameworks (SLSA 4).

L2: Configures automated pipeline stages for linting, unit testing, and artifact building.
Secures build environments using injected repository secrets rather than hardcoded credentials.
Tags release artifacts with immutable commit SHAs or semantic version numbers.
L3: Implements zero-downtime blue/green or rolling deployment strategies with automated health check gates.
Automates immediate rollback procedures when post-deployment smoke tests or health probes fail.
Separates continuous integration builds from continuous deployment release manifests.
L4: Implements progressive traffic-splitting canary releases utilizing metric-based analysis (e.g. error rate, p99 latency).
Signs container images and validates cryptographic provenance in CI prior to cluster deployment.
Optimizes pipeline execution speed utilizing remote Docker layer caching and parallelized test matrices.
L5: Architects self-service developer platform pipelines that provision ephemeral preview environments on pull requests.
Establishes enterprise-wide software supply chain security standards compliance (SLSA Level 3+).

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose a CI build takes 30 minutes because dependencies are re-downloaded on every commit; talk me through how you would optimize that pipeline.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you designed a deployment pipeline to release updates with zero downtime and automated rollbacks if errors spike.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you implemented a progressive canary deployment strategy with automated analysis across a high-traffic production service.

skills.name: Cloud Infrastructure & IaC
skills.description: Provisions scalable cloud resources using Terraform, OpenTofu, or Pulumi; manages state locking, module reusability, and drift detection.
skills.rubric_l1: Clicks around in cloud provider web consoles; creates unmanaged cloud resources without version control.
skills.rubric_l2: Writes monolithic Terraform files with hardcoded variables; struggles with state locking, remote backends, and secret isolation.
skills.rubric_l3: Develops modular, reusable IaC with remote state locking, least-privilege IAM roles, VPC isolation, and automated plan reviews.
skills.rubric_l4: Implements continuous drift detection, automated policy-as-code enforcement (OPA, Sentinel), and zero-trust VPC peering topologies.
skills.rubric_l5: Architects multi-region cloud disaster recovery failover architectures, cloud landing zones, and automated finops cost governance.

L2: Defines standard cloud compute and storage resources using structured Infrastructure as Code manifests.
Configures remote state backends (e.g. S3 with DynamoDB locking or GCS) to enable safe team collaboration.
Applies parameterization using input variables and environment-specific variable files.
L3: Authors reusable, composable Terraform modules with validated input types and explicit outputs.
Implements least-privilege IAM roles and service account permissions adhering to security best practices.
Designs secure VPC network topologies separating public edge load balancers from private database subnets.
L4: Builds automated policy-as-code pipelines using Open Policy Agent (OPA) to prevent insecure infrastructure changes.
Detects and reconciles infrastructure state drift across multiple accounts without service interruption.
Architects multi-region VPC peering and transit gateway routing with private service endpoints.
L5: Architects enterprise landing zones with automated account vending, governance guardrails, and compliance guardrails.
Develops automated disaster recovery failover pipelines capable of reprovisioning entire cloud environments in minutes.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose your team needs to manage cloud servers using Terraform; talk me through why and how you would configure remote state locking.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you handled a situation where manual console changes caused unexpected Terraform state drift in a production environment.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you architected a multi-account cloud landing zone with automated security policy guardrails.

skills.name: Containers & Kubernetes
skills.description: Architects container lifecycles, Docker multi-stage builds, Kubernetes controllers, Helm charts, Ingress, HPA, and node scheduling.
skills.rubric_l1: Runs fat container images containing build tools and secrets; does not understand pod lifecycles or container limits.
skills.rubric_l2: Writes standard Dockerfiles and basic Kubernetes Deployment YAMLs but misconfigures CPU/memory requests, limits, and probes.
skills.rubric_l3: Authors slim multi-stage container images, configures accurate liveness/readiness probes, resource limits, and Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA).
skills.rubric_l4: Diagnoses node pressure, crashloopbackoffs, OOMKilled events; designs PodDisruptionBudgets, node affinities, and custom operators.
skills.rubric_l5: Architects multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters, custom CRDs and admission controllers, and eBPF-based service mesh networks (Cilium/Istio).

L2: Constructs multi-stage Dockerfiles that eliminate build toolchains from final production runtime images.
Explains the difference between Kubernetes Pods, Deployments, and Services.
Configures basic CPU and memory resource requests and limits on container manifests.
L3: Configures liveness, readiness, and startup probes to prevent traffic routing to unready or deadlocked pods.
Implements Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) responding accurately to CPU, memory, and custom Prometheus metrics.
Manages application configuration and secrets using ConfigMaps, Secrets, and volume mounts.
L4: Diagnoses complex cluster issues including OOMKilled pods, node disk pressure, and CrashLoopBackOff states.
Enforces high availability using PodDisruptionBudgets, topology spread constraints, and anti-affinity rules.
Authors modular Helm charts or Kustomize overlays supporting multiple staging and production clusters.
L5: Authors custom Kubernetes Operators and Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) automating stateful application operations.
Architects multi-tenant cluster isolation using network policies, admission webhooks, and eBPF network layers.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose a containerized app keeps restarting immediately after deployment in Kubernetes; talk me through how you would inspect and diagnose the issue.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you tuned Kubernetes CPU/memory requests and Horizontal Pod Autoscaling for a service facing sudden traffic spikes.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you designed a multi-tenant Kubernetes cluster topology that enforced strict resource and network isolation across teams.

skills.name: Observability & Incident Response
skills.description: Implements metrics, structured logging, distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry), SLO/SLA error budgets, and incident command protocols.
skills.rubric_l1: No centralized logging; logs in raw unparsed text; learns of outages only when customers complain on social media.
skills.rubric_l2: Sets up standard dashboards (CPU/RAM usage) and high-volume alerts; suffers from alert fatigue and lacks distributed tracing.
skills.rubric_l3: Instruments OpenTelemetry tracing, RED/USE metrics, structured JSON logs with trace correlation, and actionable symptom-based alerts.
skills.rubric_l4: Defines SLIs/SLOs and error budget burn rate alerting; leads live incident triage calls and executes blameless post-mortems.
skills.rubric_l5: Architects automated incident self-healing (auto-remediation), proactive chaos engineering experiments, and enterprise reliability culture.

L2: Formats application logs as structured JSON containing timestamps, log levels, and contextual metadata.
Interprets basic telemetry dashboards visualizing request rates, error codes, and server resource usage.
Differentiates between metric gauges, counters, and histograms in monitoring tools.
L3: Instruments OpenTelemetry distributed tracing to trace request lifecycles across microservice boundaries.
Configures symptom-based alerts tied to customer impact rather than noisy internal resource fluctuations.
Participates effectively in on-call rotations and systematic incident triage workflows.
L4: Establishes Service Level Indicators (SLIs) and multi-window burn rate alerts on critical user journeys.
Analyzes distributed trace flame graphs to isolate downstream latency bottlenecks and database lock stalls.
Conducts thorough, blameless post-mortem investigations producing preventative remediation tickets.
L5: Designs automated self-healing mechanisms that isolate or restart malfunctioning service dependencies during incidents.
Executes automated chaos engineering fault injection in production to validate resilience assumptions.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose your service is throwing intermittent 500 errors; talk me through how structured logging and correlation IDs help you isolate the root cause.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you overhauled a noisy alerting system to eliminate alert fatigue while ensuring critical incidents were caught immediately.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you led the response to a major production outage where telemetry data was contradictory or incomplete.

skills.name: Linux & Networking Fundamentals
skills.description: Masters Linux kernel primitives, systemd, process signals, DNS resolution, TCP/IP stack tuning, TLS certificates, and firewalls.
skills.rubric_l1: Struggles with basic shell commands and file permissions; does not understand DNS lookup sequence or IP routing.
skills.rubric_l2: Navigates Linux file systems and inspects top/ps output but cannot debug network packet drops, DNS caching, or TLS handshake errors.
skills.rubric_l3: Debugs network connectivity using tcpdump/curl/dig, inspects systemd unit states, manages file permissions (chmod/chown), and provisions TLS certs.
skills.rubric_l4: Tunes Linux kernel sysctl parameters (tcp_tw_reuse, file-max, somaxconn), analyzes strace/lsof outputs, and debugs MTU/routing issues.
skills.rubric_l5: Leverages eBPF programs for kernel tracing and packet filtering; designs BGP peering and Software-Defined Networking (SDN) topologies.

L2: Navigates Linux directories, modifies file permissions, and manages background processes using signals (SIGTERM, SIGKILL).
Traces DNS resolution flows from local resolver cache to authoritative nameservers using dig/nslookup.
Inspects open network ports and listening sockets using netstat/ss commands.
L3: Captures and analyzes network packets using tcpdump or Wireshark to isolate connection resets and latency spikes.
Manages daemon lifecycles, log outputs, and restart policies using systemd unit files.
Configures TLS/SSL certificates and diagnoses handshake negotiation and certificate authority chain errors.
L4: Tunes Linux kernel networking parameters (sysctl somaxconn, ephemeral port ranges) to support high-throughput network services.
Uses strace, lsof, and vmstat to diagnose disk I/O bottlenecks and stalled system calls.
Troubleshoots network routing, subnet masking, and MTU packet fragmentation across cloud VPC networks.
L5: Develops custom eBPF kernel probes for real-time security auditing and network traffic shaping.
Architects BGP routing and software-defined network fabrics interconnecting hybrid on-premise and cloud datacenters.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose a server cannot connect to an external API endpoint; talk me through the step-by-step commands you use to isolate whether it is DNS, firewall, or application failure.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through a time you used tools like strace, tcpdump, or system logs to diagnose a low-level Linux performance or networking issue.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you tuned Linux kernel socket and networking parameters to handle hundreds of thousands of concurrent client connections.

skills.name: Project & Experience Deep-Dive
skills.description: Structured walkthrough of the candidate's own projects and work: scope, ownership, architecture decisions, trade-offs, and outcomes. Follow-ups probe what the candidate actually said they built.
skills.rubric_l1: Cannot describe any project coherently; vague about own role, stack, or outcome; claims work without substance.
skills.rubric_l2: Describes a project at surface level; can name the stack and own tasks but struggles with design decisions, trade-offs, or measurable outcomes.
skills.rubric_l3: Clearly explains a real project: goal, architecture, own ownership, technologies used, and key trade-offs with reasons; can dive one level deeper on any part when probed.
skills.rubric_l4: Deep command of own work: quantified outcomes, alternatives considered, failure modes handled, and how constraints shaped the design; connects project decisions to broader engineering principles.
skills.rubric_l5: Exceptional narrative and reflection: articulates the business/technical context, led non-trivial trade-offs, mentors others through the reasoning, and honestly separates team work from individual contribution.

l2: Names the project goal, stack, and their own tasks.
l3: Explains the architecture and their specific ownership area.
Justifies key design or technology choices with trade-offs.
l4: Quantifies outcomes or impact (performance, scale, users, grades of improvement).
Handles a follow-up on any component they described without hand-waving.
l5: Reflects on what they would change with hindsight and why.

question_patterns.anchor: Walk me through the most significant project you have built or contributed to — what it does, your role, and the stack you chose.
question_patterns.anchor_alt: Pick any project, class assignment, or hackathon you enjoyed — what did you build and what did you personally work on?
question_patterns.escalation: If that project had to serve 10x the users or data tomorrow, what would break first and what would you change?
probes: Why did you choose that stack over the alternatives you considered?
What was the hardest bug or setback in that project, and how did you resolve it?
Which part are you proudest of, and which part would you rebuild differently now?
How did you verify it actually worked — tests, metrics, or user feedback?
